why: Reads as a named three-item list, but the parts follow from how any argument opens, develops and closes; the distractors belong to other document types.
What a thesis statement must be follows from an essay needing a defensible central claim; the distractors fail that on inspection.
'Unity' is self-describing — one controlling idea — and the wrong options are recognisably about length or style instead.
Turns on the discourse relation each connector expresses, which a competent reader reasons out rather than recalls from a list.
A term of art, but 'marshalling' implies ordering and the distractors contradict what persuasive arrangement is for.
Register is judged by spotting slang and fillers in the options — a reading judgement, not a memorised rule.
A best-course-of-action item; the answer follows from why planning and a word limit exist.
The conclusion's purpose follows from its position in the argument; introducing new arguments is visibly inconsistent with closing.
Follows from what coherence means — the wrong options describe the absence of linkage.
'Topic sentence' is transparent and its role follows from paragraph unity, already a reasoned concept.
Choosing the sequence-opening connector is reasoning about ordering relations, not recall of a fixed list.
Cause-effect versus contrast versus time is a distinction in the connectors' meanings, worked out not memorised.
A prescriptive convention of formal register, but it follows from formality avoiding casual shortenings; the distractors lower register further.
Applies the thesis concept to four candidates — the arguable, specific claim is identified by reasoning.
A named technique, though the word 'climactic' itself implies building to the strongest point last.
A labelled technique whose answer follows from the funnel metaphor of broad narrowing to specific.
Best-course-of-action item; fair rebuttal follows from what makes an argument credible.
Follows from the body being where the argument is actually developed; no allocation figures to recall.
